overview: Licensing Commission Chairperson Robert Delafano detailed the city's liquor licensing categories, application procedures, and enforcement protocols. The discussion covered current license availability, fee structures, and the commission's role in supporting local businesses while maintaining public safety.

items.title: Introduction and background
items.summary: John Petrella introduced Robert Delafano, Chairperson of the Medford Licensing Commission, who discussed his history as a Medford native and his 36-year career with the city fire department.

items.title: Commission membership and schedule
items.summary: Delafano described the Commission’s monthly public meeting schedule and introduced its members, highlighting their professional backgrounds in finance, construction, and administration.

items.title: Categories of retail liquor licenses
items.summary: The Commission categorized retail liquor licenses into four types based on the alcohol served and differentiated between on-premise pouring, one-day events, and package store licenses.

items.title: One-day license regulations
items.summary: Delafano explained the regulations for Section 14 one-day licenses, which require liability insurance and are limited to 30 per person annually.

items.title: Package store license cap
items.summary: The Chairperson confirmed that Medford has reached its state-allotted limit of 12 package store licenses, meaning new stores can only open via license transfers.

items.title: License application process
items.summary: Delafano outlined the application process for new licenses, which involves local approval followed by a mandatory investigation by the state Alcoholic Beverage Control Commission (ABCC).

items.title: Fee schedule and entertainment licenses
items.summary: The Commission reviewed the fee schedule, including $2,000 annual fees for all-alcohol restaurant licenses and $100 per category for entertainment devices and performances.

items.title: License availability and population limits
items.summary: Delafano reported that 28 all-alcohol on-premise licenses are currently available in Medford and clarified how population census data determines state-allotted quotas.

items.title: Violations and enforcement
items.summary: The Commission detailed grounds for license non-renewal or violation, including drug convictions, strict November renewal deadlines, and over-serving intoxicated persons.

items.title: Compliance checks and education
items.summary: Delafano described police-led compliance checks using underage agents and mandatory annual educational sessions held for all city licensees to ensure regulatory compliance.

items.title: Market value of license transfers
items.summary: The Chairperson discussed the legality of transferring licenses during business sales, noting that their market value increases significantly only when no new licenses are available from the city.

subject: Liquor License Regulations and Application Procedures
